# Product Requirements Document (Seed Draft)

**Product:** Trader Bookkeeper
**Version:** 0.1 (hackathon MVP)
**Status:** Seed input for the Devpost Learn Skill Pack. Use this to answer the Skill Pack's prompts. The official `prd.md` in the repo must be the one **generated by the Skill Pack** and then edited to match this.

---

## 1. Summary

Trader Bookkeeper is an offline, free, voice-first mobile app that lets informal market traders record daily sales and expenses by speaking or typing, review them, and produce a monthly income report that can support a loan application.

## 2. Problem

Informal traders keep records in their heads or on scraps of paper. As a result:
- They often do not know their true daily or monthly profit.
- They cannot show proof of income, so microfinance lenders and cooperatives are hard to access.
- Existing bookkeeping apps assume accounting knowledge, a steady connection, a capable phone and a subscription fee, which do not match their reality.

## 3. Goals

1. A trader can record a day's sales and expenses in under 2 minutes by speaking or typing in plain language.
2. The trader always sees and approves what is saved.
3. The app works with no internet, no account and no cost.
4. The app runs smoothly on a low-end Android phone.
5. At month end the trader can produce a clear one-page income report.

## 4. Non-Goals (MVP)

User accounts, cloud sync, multi-user shops, inventory management, payments or bank integration, multi-currency, tax filing, trading advice, forex or investment tracking.

## 5. Target Users

**Primary persona: "Mama Ngozi," market trader**
- Sells `<trader type to be chosen, e.g. provisions or food items>` in a local market.
- Age 30 to 55, uses a low-end Android phone, limited data, speaks English and Pidgin, may prefer speaking to typing.
- Tracks money mentally or on paper. Wants to know if she is making profit and wants access to a small loan to restock.

**Secondary persona: "Emeka," young shop assistant or helper**
- Records sales for an owner at the end of the day.
- Comfortable with phones, wants a fast way to log entries.

**Indirect user: Lender or cooperative officer**
- Receives the report and wants a clear, consistent summary of income.

## 6. User Stories

| ID | As a... | I want to... | So that... |
|---|---|---|---|
| US-1 | trader | speak my day's sales and expenses | I do not have to type or learn accounting |
| US-2 | trader | type my entries if speaking does not work | I can always record |
| US-3 | trader | see what the app understood and fix mistakes before saving | my records are correct |
| US-4 | trader | see today's sales, expenses and profit | I know how my day went |
| US-5 | trader | hear a spoken summary | I do not need to read |
| US-6 | trader | look back at previous days | I can check past records |
| US-7 | trader | generate a monthly report | I can show a lender my income |
| US-8 | trader | use the app with no internet and no payment | it fits my budget and situation |
| US-9 | trader | use phrases I normally use, including Pidgin | the app feels natural |
| US-10 | evaluator | try the app without a microphone | I can test the full flow quickly |

## 7. Functional Requirements

### Recording
- **FR-1:** The Record screen has a microphone button and a text input.
- **FR-2:** The user can speak or type one or more sentences describing sales and expenses.
- **FR-3:** If speech is unavailable or permission is denied, the app explains this and focuses the text input.

### Parsing
- **FR-4:** The parser converts text into entries with type (sale or expense), item, quantity, unit, unit price and total.
- **FR-5:** The parser understands amounts such as `40k`, `40 thousand`, `15,000`, `₦15000`, and small number words.
- **FR-6:** The parser understands common Pidgin phrasing such as `I sell am`, `I don sell`, `I buy`.
- **FR-7:** Words like `each` or `per` mean a unit price, and the total is calculated by code.
- **FR-8:** Multiple entries in one sentence are split into separate entries.
- **FR-9:** Anything the parser cannot read is shown as an editable entry, never silently dropped.
- **FR-10:** The parser is implemented in plain code with an automated test suite of at least 30 cases.

### Confirmation
- **FR-11:** Parsed entries appear on a Confirm screen as editable cards.
- **FR-12:** The user can edit type, item, quantity, unit price, total and date, and delete any entry.
- **FR-13:** Low-confidence or incomplete entries are visually highlighted.
- **FR-14:** Entries cannot be saved without a total.
- **FR-15:** Nothing is saved until the user taps Save.

### Ledger
- **FR-16:** The Today screen lists the day's entries with total sales, total expenses and profit.
- **FR-17:** The user can edit or delete a saved entry.
- **FR-18:** The History screen lists previous days with their profit and opens a day's detail.
- **FR-19:** All totals are calculated by code from stored entries.

### Spoken summary
- **FR-20:** A Listen button reads the day's summary aloud.

### Report
- **FR-21:** The user chooses a month and previews a one-page report.
- **FR-22:** The report includes trader and business name, month, total sales, total expenses, net profit, active days, average daily sales, top items, top expenses and a daily chart.
- **FR-23:** The report includes a signature line and a note that it is self-recorded and not independently audited.
- **FR-24:** The report can be exported as a PDF and shared through the phone's share sheet.

### Demo mode
- **FR-25:** Demo mode offers tappable sample sentences that go through the normal flow.
- **FR-26:** Demo mode can load a sample month of data so the report can be viewed immediately.
- **FR-27:** Demo data is clearly labeled and kept separate from real data.

### Settings
- **FR-28:** The user can enter trader name, business name and trader type.
- **FR-29:** The user can choose the speech engine (when more than one is available) and toggle demo mode.

## 8. Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| NFR-1 | All core features work in airplane mode |
| NFR-2 | No API key, account or payment is required |
| NFR-3 | Runs on low-end Android (tested on Infinix Smart 7) |
| NFR-4 | Parsing a typical sentence takes under 50 ms; the app starts in under 4 seconds |
| NFR-5 | Large tap targets, high contrast, clear icons, minimal text |
| NFR-6 | Data stays on the device; no tracking or analytics |
| NFR-7 | The app does not crash on empty, garbled or unexpected input |
| NFR-8 | Money is handled as integers and never as floating point |
| NFR-9 | The APK does not bundle large models |

## 9. AI Requirements

- **AI-1:** The project is built using the Devpost Learn Skill Pack with GitHub Copilot.
- **AI-2:** Speech recognition is the main AI element in the app. Prefer an on-device model if the speech test on the Infinix Smart 7 shows acceptable speed and accuracy. Otherwise use the built-in recognizer.
- **AI-3 (stretch):** An optional on-device small language model handles sentences the rule-based parser cannot read. It is downloaded on demand and the app works fully without it.
- **AI-4:** AI never performs arithmetic or saves data without user confirmation.

## 10. Acceptance Criteria (Key Scenarios)

**Scenario 1: voice entry**
- Given the app is in airplane mode, when the user says "sold 3 bags of rice at 40k each, paid transport 5k", then the Confirm screen shows a sale of rice (qty 3, unit price 40,000, total 120,000) and an expense of transport (5,000), and after saving, Today shows sales 120,000, expenses 5,000 and profit 115,000.

**Scenario 2: Pidgin entry**
- Given the user types "I don sell 2 carton indomie for 15 thousand", then a sale of indomie with quantity 2 cartons and total 15,000 is shown.

**Scenario 3: unclear input**
- Given the user types "I sell am 40k", then a sale with total 40,000 is shown, the item field is highlighted as missing, and the user can fill it in.

**Scenario 4: garbled input**
- Given the text cannot be parsed, then the app shows an editable blank entry and does not crash.

**Scenario 5: report**
- Given a month with recorded entries, when the user opens Report and chooses that month, then a one-page report shows correct totals and can be shared as a PDF.

**Scenario 6: demo mode**
- Given demo mode is on and no microphone is used, the user can complete the full flow from sample sentence to PDF report.

**Scenario 7: speech unavailable**
- Given microphone permission is denied, the app explains how to enable it and lets the user type instead.

## 11. Success Metrics (for the hackathon and a pilot)

- Parser passes 90% or more of the test suite
- Full flow works on the Infinix Smart 7 in airplane mode
- A first-time user records a day's entries unassisted in under 2 minutes
- At least one real trader tries the app and gives feedback
- Report totals match manual calculation in all test months

## 12. Constraints

- Build window: October 6 to October 25, 2026 (hard deadline October 26, 2026, 5:00 pm Eastern Time)
- Team of two
- No paid services
- Public repository with an open source license
- Demo video under 3 minutes

## 13. Assumptions

- Traders have an Android phone with a working microphone.
- Many traders are more comfortable speaking than typing, but some phones or accents will make speech unreliable, so typed input is required.
- A self-reported income report is useful to some microfinance lenders and cooperatives as supporting information, but is not a guarantee of loan approval.

## 14. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Speech recognition poor on the target phone or for Pidgin | Early speech test, typed input, tolerant parser, confirm screen |
| On-device models too slow or too large | Treat as optional; fall back to the built-in recognizer |
| Parser misses unusual phrasing | Large test set, unclear-entry handling, easy manual edit |
| Native libraries complicate the build | Test a development build early |
| Time pressure with two people | Strict cut order; feature freeze on October 22 |
